value_domain: Australian financial year (1 July to 30 June)
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23
variable_description: The financial year the edited income amounts on the row refer to, running 1 July to 30 June. Every table in this product covers a single year, so the column is constant within a table and only earns its keep once several years are stacked into a panel. It is the anchor for every amount beside it: the income measures are annual totals for this year, not point-in-time figures, and the person's age or address is not necessarily measured on the same basis.
value_definition: A financial year label rather than a date, one value per table. The ABS builds the income measures on a financial-year basis because they come from annual tax records.
limitation: It says nothing about when in the year income was received, so it cannot be used to place a job start, a retirement or a business failure inside the year. A person who appears in consecutive years has not necessarily been in scope throughout, since lodgment and employer reporting decide entry to the file each year.
rationale: The ABS methodology for the income series that this product is drawn from describes financial-year releases built from annual tax records, which fixes the reference period the column carries.
evidence_quote: The current release includes data for the five financial years between 2018-19 and 2022-23.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Reference financial year' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying that the value is constant within a table.

value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23
variable_description: A marker the ABS attaches to the row, recording that the income measures in this table are ABS constructions rather than raw tax return labels. That distinction is the whole point of the product: each amount beside it is built by mapping a set of tax items into an income concept, a step the ABS warns is imperfect because "the Australian tax system is purpose-built and complex, and in some cases it is difficult to determine how a particular income tax item should be used to describe income standards". The column is the flag for that processing, not an amount.
value_definition: A short indicator rather than a dollar figure. No published code list gives the meaning of its individual values.
limitation: It cannot tell you which income item was derived, imputed or corrected, nor what the underlying tax return figure was, so it is no substitute for the raw ITR product when a specific label is needed. Because its values are undocumented, it should not be used as a data quality filter.
rationale: No published page defines this column. The reading comes from the custodian's wording, from the table name, and from the ABS methodology describing how the income categories in this family are derived from tax items.
evidence_quote: Conceptual misalignment. The Australian tax system is purpose-built and complex, and in some cases it is difficult to determine how a particular income tax item should be used to describe income standards, and in some cases the item can be a partial conceptual match.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Income derived variable by abs' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said whether the column was an amount or a marker.

value_domain: Annual investment income, ABS derived (dollars, may be negative)
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: What a person earned from their savings and assets in the year: interest, dividends with the franking credit attached, trust distributions, and rent. The ABS builds it from the tax return items for gross interest, franked and unfranked dividends, the franking credit, non-primary-production trust shares and distributions, New Zealand franking credits, net rent and net foreign rent. Rent and trust shares enter net of expenses, so a negatively geared landlord can drag the whole figure below zero even in a year of strong interest and dividends.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the financial year, gross of tax but net of rental and trust expenses, and grossed up by franking credits. It can be negative, and the ABS treats a negative value as income from the source rather than as missing.
limitation: It is not a return on wealth, because it mixes a gross flow (interest) with a net one (rent) and because a person's assets are nowhere in this file. Net capital gains are excluded, so a year of large realised gains can leave investment income looking flat.
rationale: The ABS methodology lists the exact tax return items that make up investment income in this family of measures and states that all values are gross pre-tax dollars.
evidence_quote: All monetary values are presented as gross pre-tax dollars, wherever possible.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Investment income amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said which tax items feed it or that it can be negative.

value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Counts of individuals
variable_description: Whether the person counts as having investment income in the year, which in ABS usage includes people whose investment income was negative. The rule is explicit: "The number of individuals for each income source includes all persons with either positive or negative net income from that source." So a landlord who lost money on a rental property and a retiree living on term deposit interest are both flagged here, and the flag exists because a simple test of INVINC being above zero would drop the first of them.
value_definition: A short indicator, not an amount, derived from the investment income measure on the same row. It marks presence of the income type rather than its size or sign.
limitation: It cannot separate a large portfolio from a single interest-bearing account, and it does not distinguish gain from loss, so counting flagged people as investors overstates active investing. People below the lodgment threshold with modest interest income are missing from the file entirely, so the flag understates how widespread small investment income is.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines how individuals are counted against each income source, including the treatment of negative net income, which is the rule this flag implements.
evidence_quote: The number of individuals for each income source includes all persons with either positive or negative net income from that source.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Invinc earner flag' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the inclusion of negative amounts was not stated.

value_domain: Source of the employee income amount (tax return or payment summary)
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Non-lodgers
variable_description: Where the employee income figure beside it came from: the person's own tax return, or their employer's payment summary because they did not lodge one. The ABS defines the group it identifies: "Non-lodgers are individuals who do not lodge a tax return. This can include employees who have employee income reported by their employers, persons who receive an income below certain levels (i.e. the tax-free threshold), or persons who derive their income from some Commonwealth of Australia Government pension, benefit and allowance payments that are exempt from income tax." It is the single most important control column in the table, because a payment-summary row can only ever carry employee income.
value_definition: A short code distinguishing the two sources of the employee income amount. It qualifies WANDS specifically rather than the other income measures on the row.
limitation: It flags how the income was reported, not whether the person was obliged to lodge, so it cannot be read as tax compliance. It also cannot identify non-lodgers who had no employer reporting at all, such as a self-funded retiree below the threshold, because those people never enter the file to be flagged.
rationale: The custodian's wording names the two sources, and the ABS methodology defines non-lodgers and explains that employer-reported income is what brings them into this family of measures.
evidence_quote: Non-lodgers are individuals who do not lodge a tax return. This can include employees who have employee income reported by their employers, persons who receive an income below certain levels (i.e. the tax-free threshold), or persons who derive their income from some Commonwealth of Australia Government pension, benefit and allowance payments that are exempt from income tax.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Source of wands amount (itr or ps)' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without explaining what turns on the distinction.

value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Non-lodgers
variable_description: Whether the person is in the file only because an employer reported paying them, with no tax return of their own behind the record. These people are a genuinely different population: they are typically low earners, since the ABS notes non-lodgers include "persons who receive an income below certain levels (i.e. the tax-free threshold)", and their record can contain nothing but wages. Excluding them makes a low-income sample thinner; including them without care makes total income look artificially concentrated in employment.
value_definition: A short indicator, not an amount, applied to the person for the year. It is the earner counterpart of the source code beside it.
limitation: A flagged person's investment, business and superannuation income is unknown rather than zero, so treating their total income as complete understates them by whatever they did not have to declare. The flag also moves year to year for the same person as their lodgment obligation changes, which can look like an income change in a panel.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines the non-lodger population and states that employees with employer-reported income are part of it, which is the group this flag marks.
evidence_quote: Sometimes, Individual Tax Returns are not lodged, or not all items (e.g. occupation) are completed. The ABS advises caution when interpreting data subject to high rates of missing information.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Ps-only unit earner flag' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the analytical consequence of the group was unstated.

value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: The residual income category: everything on the tax return the ABS could not place in employment, business, investment or superannuation. It is defined by exclusion - "Other income comprises income items reported on the individual income tax return that were not allocated to one of the above categories" - and mostly holds foreign pensions and annuities, controlled foreign company income, transfer or trust income and other foreign source income. The ABS does not trust it on its own account: "Other income is not published separately as it does not provide a reliable view of the category."
value_definition: A dollar amount for the financial year, gross of tax, folded into total income. Its contents depend on the mapping applied for the year rather than on a single return label.
limitation: The ABS itself says the category is not reliable enough to publish on its own, so a series built from it is weaker than one built from the four named categories. It is defined by what the other categories left behind, so a change in the mapping can move income into or out of it without anything changing in a person's affairs.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines other income by exclusion, lists the tax return items it draws on and states the publication caveat.
evidence_quote: Other income is not published separately as it does not provide a reliable view of the category. It is included in total income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Other income amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the ABS's own warning about the category was missing.

value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: Whether the person had any income in the residual category during the year. It is the flag most likely to be misread, because being flagged says only that some tax item fell outside the four named income concepts, and the underlying category is the one the ABS declines to publish separately. In practice it picks out people with foreign pensions, foreign source income or controlled foreign company income, so it works better as a marker of unusual affairs than as an income indicator.
value_definition: A short indicator, not an amount, marking presence of income in the residual category for the person and year.
limitation: Because the category is a remainder, the flag is not stable in meaning across years: an item reclassified into employment or investment income stops flagging people without any change in what they received. It should not be used as a proxy for having a foreign income source, since not everything in the category is foreign.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines the residual category and its contents, which is what this flag marks; the publication caveat on the category applies equally to the flag.
evidence_quote: Other income comprises income items reported on the individual income tax return that were not allocated to one of the above categories.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Othinc earner flag' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, with nothing about the residual nature of the category.

value_domain: Annual own unincorporated business income, ABS derived (dollars, may be negative)
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: What a sole trader or partner made from their own business in the year, after expenses but before tax. The ABS defines it as "the profit or loss that accrues to owners of, or partners in, their own unincorporated businesses", and treats a bad year as negative income: "Losses occur when operating expenses are greater than receipts and are treated as negative income." The custodian's label reads 'incorporated', which inverts the concept - income from an incorporated business the person works in is employee income, not this.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the financial year, net of operating expenses, depreciation and reportable superannuation contributions but before income tax. It is built from the net business income, personal services income, partnership distribution and primary-production trust items on the tax return.
limitation: It is not a measure of self-employment in general, because working directors of their own companies are classified as employees and their income sits in the employee measure instead. Non-primary-production trust distributions are deliberately left out, so a person running a business through a discretionary trust can show nothing here.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines the concept, lists the tax return items behind it, states the treatment of losses and states explicitly that incorporated business owners are excluded.
evidence_quote: It also excludes the income of working directors/owners of incorporated businesses who are classified as employees; consequently their income is included under Wage and salary income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Own incorporated business income amount', which states the opposite of the concept, and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice.

value_domain: Own unincorporated business income earner indicator
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: Whether the person had income or a loss from their own unincorporated business in the year. Loss-making owners are flagged as earners, because the ABS treats a loss as negative income rather than as an absence of income, which makes this the closest thing in the table to a count of sole traders and partners. It is also the flag that moves the aggregate figure around most, since a small number of large business losses can pull the mean well below the median.
value_definition: A short indicator, not an amount, marking presence of unincorporated business income of either sign for the person and year.
limitation: It counts people, not businesses, so a partnership of four is four flagged people and a person running two businesses is one. It also misses anyone operating through a company or a discretionary trust, so it undercounts small business owners rather than measuring them.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines the income concept, states that losses are treated as negative income, and sets out how individuals are counted against an income source.
evidence_quote: Losses occur when operating expenses are greater than receipts and are treated as negative income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Ownuninc earner flag' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said that loss-makers are included.

value_domain: Annual superannuation and annuity income, ABS derived (dollars)
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: Superannuation and annuity income the person declared for tax. The ABS builds it from the annuity and income stream labels, superannuation lump sums, life insurance bonuses and, from 2018-19, released First home super saver amounts. The measure has a hole in the middle of it by design: "From 1 July 2007, people aged 60 years and over who receive superannuation income in the form of a lump sum or income stream (such as a pension) from a taxed source, receive that income tax free", and the ABS concludes that its superannuation statistics "are regarded as partial, subject to under-coverage".
value_definition: A dollar amount for the financial year, drawn only from amounts that reach a tax return. It mixes regular income stream payments with one-off lump sums, so a single year's figure can be dominated by a withdrawal.
limitation: It cannot measure retirement income, because the largest group of retirees - people over 60 drawing on a taxed source - has nothing to declare and often lodges no return at all. The ABS points to survey data for a fuller picture, and the gap grows with age, so comparing superannuation income across age groups in this column compares coverage as much as income.
rationale: The ABS methodology lists the tax return items in the concept and states in the same section why the measure under-covers superannuation income after 2007.
evidence_quote: Due to the above reason, the superannuation statistics (persons, income) included in this release are regarded as partial, subject to under-coverage.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Superannuation and annuity income amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the under-coverage that dominates this column was unstated.

value_domain: Superannuation and annuity income earner indicator
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: Whether the person declared superannuation or annuity income in the year, which marks taxable superannuation rather than superannuation income in general. A 62-year-old on an account-based pension from a taxed fund is not flagged, because the income is tax free and never reaches a return, while a 58-year-old on the same pension is. The flag therefore tracks the tax treatment and the person's age far more than it tracks retirement.
value_definition: A short indicator, not an amount, marking presence of superannuation or annuity income for the person and year.
limitation: Using it to date retirement will systematically place people too early, because the flag tends to switch off at 60 exactly when the person's superannuation income becomes their main support. It also fires for a one-off lump sum withdrawal by someone still working full time.
rationale: The ABS methodology explains the post-2007 tax treatment that removes most superannuation income from tax records, which determines who this flag can and cannot mark.
evidence_quote: From 1 July 2007, people aged 60 years and over who receive superannuation income in the form of a lump sum or income stream (such as a pension) from a taxed source, receive that income tax free.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Supinc earner flag' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the age discontinuity that drives the flag was not mentioned.

value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The person whose year of income the row summarises, and the key that turns these annual totals into a person's income history when the year tables are stacked. Each table holds one row per person per financial year, so this column is what makes a panel possible and what carries an income measure out to the same person's Census, health and payment records. ABS holds the joining information apart from the data itself, through a "Person Linkage Spine" that links datasets "separate from the main body of data".
value_definition: An opaque synthetic number, one value per person, consistent across the tables of this product. In fplida the values are generated rather than derived from anyone.
limitation: A person missing from a year's table has not necessarily had no income, because entry to the file depends on lodging a return or having an employer report payments. The key is a person, not a household or a family, so partner and household income cannot be assembled from it without a separate relationship source.
rationale: ABS describes the PLIDA spine and its separation from the data, which is what this key is; the structure of the product, one row per person per year, is visible in the registry's own table list.
evidence_quote: The Person Linkage Spine allows us to link datasets through a spine of key information, separate from the main body of data.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Individual encrypted scrambled identifier' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so nothing said the column is what makes the annual tables into a panel.

value_domain: Annual total income, ABS derived (dollars, may be negative)
value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: The person's whole market income for the year, and the one column in this table that is a sum rather than a component. The ABS defines it as "the sum of all reported income derived from Employee income, Own unincorporated business, Superannuation, Investments and Other income", and then names what it leaves out: "Government pensions, benefits or allowances are excluded from the ABS income data and do not appear in Other income or Total income." The ABS puts that missing piece at between 9% and 11% of total income on survey estimates.
value_definition: A dollar amount for the financial year, gross of tax and before the Medicare levy, and equal to the five income components on the same row. It can be negative where business or investment losses exceed other income.
limitation: It is market income, not the money a person had to live on, so a pensioner shows near zero and a benefit recipient shows only their earnings. Adding a pension estimate to it will double-count for people whose payments were taxable and already declared through the components.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines total income as the sum of the five components used in this product and states in the same passage that government payments are excluded, with an order of magnitude for the exclusion.
evidence_quote: Government pensions, benefits or allowances are excluded from the ABS income data and do not appear in Other income or Total income.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Total income amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the exclusion of government payments, which is the main thing a reader needs, was missing.

value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: Whether the person counts as an earner at all in the year, on the broadest of the definitions in this table. The ABS rule is that "anyone who earns income, whether from employment, superannuation, investment etc. is counted as an earner". It is the union of the five component flags rather than their sum, which is why the ABS warns that adding the component counts overstates the population - a person with wages, dividends and a rental property is flagged three times among the components and once here.
value_definition: A short indicator, not an amount, marking presence of any income for the person and year. It sits with the five component flags on the same row.
limitation: It cannot be used as a population denominator, because people with no taxable income and no employer reporting never enter the file to be flagged as non-earners. Someone receiving only a government pension is not an earner here, however substantial their income.
rationale: The ABS methodology gives the definition of an earner used in this family of measures and explains why counts across income sources cannot be added.
evidence_quote: In PIA, anyone who earns income, whether from employment, superannuation, investment etc. is counted as an earner.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Totalinc earner flag' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so the relationship to the five component flags was not stated.

value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: Everything the person earned for their labour in the year. The ABS defines it as "the total (or gross) income received as a return for labour from an employer or from a person's own incorporated business (when they are employed by this business)". It is wider than salary: allowances, tips and director's fees, employer lump sums, termination payments, attributed personal services income, employee share scheme discounts, reportable fringe benefits, reportable employer superannuation contributions and foreign employment income are all in it. Unlike the other income measures it does not need a tax return, because "the data used in deriving employee income comes from both ITRs and Income Statements (where an individual has not lodged an ITR)".
value_definition: A dollar amount for the financial year, gross of tax and of the Medicare levy. It includes non-cash components such as reportable fringe benefits, so it exceeds cash wages for anyone salary packaging.
limitation: It is not take-home pay and not a wage rate, since it says nothing about hours, weeks worked or the number of jobs behind it, so a low value can be a full year on low pay or a fortnight on high pay. Because it includes termination payments and employer superannuation contributions, a redundancy year can look like a pay rise.
rationale: The ABS methodology gives the definition verbatim, lists every tax return and income statement item that feeds it, and states the dual source.
evidence_quote: Employee income is the total (or gross) income received as a return for labour from an employer or from a person's own incorporated business (when they are employed by this business).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Employee income amount' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, so neither the breadth of the concept nor the payment summary source was on the page.

value_source: ABS, Personal Income in Australia methodology, 2022-23, Data Concepts
variable_description: Whether the person had employee income in the year, and the best covered flag here because employers report pay whether or not a return is lodged. That coverage is the reason to prefer it over the others for questions about who was working: a person can be missing from the investment and business measures for want of a tax return, but an employed person with a tax file number generally reaches the file through their employer.
value_definition: A short indicator, not an amount, marking presence of employee income for the person and year. It pairs with the source code on the same row, which says whether the underlying amount came from a return or a payment summary.
limitation: It is not a measure of employment during the year: an employment termination payment or a lump sum received long after a job ended will flag someone who did no work, and a person paid cash off the books will not be flagged at all. It also says nothing about full time or part time, since hours are not in this file.
rationale: The ABS methodology defines employee income and states that it is derived from income statements where no tax return was lodged, which is what gives this flag its wider coverage.
evidence_quote: The data used in deriving employee income comes from both ITRs and Income Statements (where an individual has not lodged an ITR).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's wording 'Employee income earner flag' and repeated the generic no-value-list sentence twice, without saying why its coverage differs from the other flags.
